title: Attention kernel optimization profiling — FlashAttention, paged attention, fused ops (experiment log)
content:
Summary:

This document captures the experiment log and profiling notes for attention kernel optimizations we ran between 2025-11-10 and 2025-11-27. The goal was to measure the perf and scalability impact of three implementation strategies in our serving runtime: FlashAttention, paged attention (KV paging / sparse KV memory), and operator fusion (fused matmul+softmax+dropout/backprop-friendly kernels). We focused on latency and tokens/sec for realistic serving configurations (small to mid batch sizes, variable context lengths) as well as identifying dominant bottlenecks for long-context workloads.

Goals:
- Quantify throughput (tokens/s) and p99 latency changes vs baseline for each optimization.
- Determine break-even points (sequence length, batch size) where each approach is beneficial.
- Produce clear recommendations for default runtime settings and canary rollout plan.
- Capture actionable follow-ups and perf-regression detection hooks.

Hardware & software baseline:
- GPU: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (single-GPU tests) and RTX 6000 Ada for small sanity checks.
- CPU: AMD EPYC (used for host-side paging tests).
- CUDA: 12.2, cuBLAS 12.x, cuDNN 9.x
- PyTorch: 2.2 (for reference model runs), runtime: redwood-serving-runtime v0.28.0-rc1
- FlashAttention: FlashAttention2 patched into runtime build from PR #842 (linked).
- Paged attention: experimental KV paging prototype that asynchronously pages old KV pages to host pinned memory and streams back on demand.
- Fused ops: custom fused attention kernels (matmul + softmax + dropout fused) built using Triton and custom CUDA kernels.
- Tools: nsight-systems, nsight-compute, cupy/cupti timers, NVIDIA Nsight flamegraphs, perf counters (achieved by nvprof replacement), python timeit for end-to-end.

Test matrix (representative runs):
- Models: LLaMA-2-7B (dense 32k context enabled), Llama-2-7B-quant (int8 simulated), Mistral-7B for cross-arch sanity.
- Sequence lengths: 128, 512, 2048, 8192, 32768 (where memory allows; for very long context we used paged attention).
- Batch sizes: 1, 2, 4, 8 (typical serving range).
- Request patterns: steady stream single-request-per-batch (low concurrency), bursty concurrent requests (simulate PLG spikes).
- Metrics recorded: median latency, p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization (SM%), memory bandwidth usage, kernel launch counts, time spent in attention kernels vs GEMM/softmax/transpose/other kernels.

Baseline observations (v0.27 runtime, no FlashAttention / no fused ops / no paging):
- For seq <= 512, attention accounted for ~35-45% of token latency; majority of time spent in cuBLAS GEMM (Q*K^T, Q*V) and high-frequency small kernel launches that add scheduling overhead.
- For seq 2k-8k, memory bandwidth and KV-cache scatter/gather overheads dominate; large increase in host<->device activity when KV cache size grows beyond GPU memory (runtime currently errors out).
- Kernel launch overhead was visible for batch sizes <= 2 and short sequences: many small CUDA kernels (transpose, reduce, softmax) cost scheduling latency that hurts p99.

FlashAttention experiments:
- Implementation: integrated FlashAttention2 as fused attention path for standard dense attention when sequence length and model dtype meet preconditions (float16/bfloat16, contiguous QKV layout).
- Runs: LLaMA-2-7B, seq 128/512/2048, batch 1/4.
- Results (approx):
  - seq128, batch1: tokens/sec +22% vs baseline, median latency -15%, p99 -8%
  - seq512, batch1: tokens/sec +35%, median latency -28%, p99 -20%
  - seq2048, batch1: tokens/sec +18%, median latency -12%
- Profiling notes: FlashAttention reduces peak memory usage significantly (no separate Q*K matmul allocation + better memory access patterns). Kernel time dominated by a single large fused kernel, reducing kernel launch counts by ~6x. SM utilization improved and warp efficiency higher.
- Limitations: for extremely long contexts (>=8k) FlashAttention still requires the whole KV to be present on-device and hits memory limits; no inherent paging. Also FlashAttention performance depends on contiguous memory layout; nonstandard layout in some model shims required small data copies that reduced gains (~5%).

Paged attention experiments (KV paging prototype):
- Implementation: maintain active working set of KV pages on GPU; older pages are migrated to host pinned memory asynchronously. When a request needs older context, we stream back required pages with overlapping compute. Uses cudaMemcpyAsync and host pinned staging buffers; prefetch heuristics implemented (LRU + warmup).
- Runs: LLaMA-2-7B, seq 8192 and 32768, batch 1 only (batching with long context is rare).
- Results (approx):
  - seq8192, batch1: end-to-end latency ~2.6x baseline (baseline could not run due to OOM), tokens/sec when sustained ~40-55% of flashattention-short-run throughput for <=2048; depends strongly on prefetch hit rate.
  - seq32768: feasible with paging, but p99 spikes large on cold misses (10x single-page load cost).
- Profiling notes: dominant cost when cold is PCIe/NVLink transfer latency and CPU-driven staging. When prefetch hit-rate >90% (warm steady-state), compute overlapped with transfers and effective throughput improved; however p99 remained high due to occasional misses.
- Observed contention: host CPU scheduling and memcpy streams saturated when multiple concurrent requests triggered page-ins. Need to limit concurrent page-ins or add a throttling policy.

Fused ops experiments (triton + custom CUDA fused matmul+softmax kernels):
- Implementation: wrote fused kernels to eliminate intermediate allocations and kernel launches for small- to medium-sized sequences, including backprop-friendly variants for eval-time caching correctness.
- Runs: seq 128-2048, batch 1-4.
- Results (approx):
  - seq128, batch1: tokens/sec +28-32% vs baseline, p99 -25%
  - seq512, batch1: tokens/sec +20%, p99 -18%
  - seq2048, batch1: marginal gains vs FlashAttention (FlashAttention slightly better due to memory access pattern optimizations).
- Profiling notes: fused ops eliminated many small kernels and reduced global memory traffic by keeping intermediate results in registers/shared memory. However, achieving consistently high occupancy required careful tuning of block sizes and register usage. For some shapes fused kernels performed worse due to register spilling.

Comparative analysis & break-evens:
- Short to medium contexts (<=512): fused ops and FlashAttention both give large wins. If model supports FlashAttention (layout + dtype) prefer FlashAttention for slightly better memory usage; otherwise enable fused ops.
- Medium contexts (512-2048): FlashAttention is typically best; fused ops still competitive and useful as fallback.
- Long contexts (>2048): FlashAttention alone is insufficient because of device memory limits. Paged attention is the only practical approach to serve 8k-32k+ contexts on single GPU. Expect higher p99 and lower tokens/sec. Hybrid approach: use paged attention with fused kernels inside each page to get best throughput.
- Small batches (1-2): kernel-launch overhead is important - fused ops and FlashAttention reduce launch counts and improve p99.
- Larger batches (>=4) amortize kernel-launch costs; GEMM/cuBLAS paths become more important and tuned cuBLAS paths should be leveraged.

Bottlenecks discovered:
- Kernel launch overhead and many small kernels (transpose, softmax) are major contributors to p99 for small batch + short seqs.
- Memory bandwidth pressure and PCIe/NVLink transfer latency dominate for paged runs; host CPU scheduling and pinned memory throughput are second-order constraints.
- Register pressure and occupancy for fused kernels require per-model autotuning; poor autotuning leads to spills that kill perf.
- Layout conversion overhead when model QKV layout differs from FlashAttention expected layout can erase gains.

Operational recommendations:
- Default runtime behavior (canary first):
  1) Enable FlashAttention path when model dtype is fp16/bf16 and QKV memory is contiguous (config flag: attention.flashattention.enabled = true). Canary rollout to 5% of hosts.
  2) Enable fused-ops fallback for models that do not meet FlashAttention preconditions.
  3) Provide paged-attention as opt-in for customers needing >8k contexts and only on Dedicated / Private where host resources can be controlled. Document p99 implications.
- Tuning and auto-config: add a per-model microbench at model load that tests sequences {128,512,2048} with batch {1,4} to automatically select attention path and kernel tuning parameters. Cache tuning decisions in model metadata.
- Prefetch/throttle: implement a prefetch policy and concurrency limits for paged-attention to avoid saturating PCIe and host memcpy. Add a soft limit on simultaneous page-ins per-GPU.
- Metrics & monitoring: emit kernel-level timing (time_in_attention_kernel, time_in_paging, page_fault_rate, prefetch_hit_rate), and add an alert when prefetch_hit_rate < 90% for long-context endpoints.

Action items / follow-ups:
- PR #842: finish FlashAttention integration tests and add layout normalization shim to avoid copies (owner: Priya) - target 2025-12-05.
- Create a small automated microbench harness in runtime that runs at model-attach time and writes tuning metadata (owner: Luca) - target 2025-12-12 (Jira ENG-1274).
- Paged attention: implement page-in concurrency throttling and add host-side bandwidth limiter (owner: Jamal) - spike complete by 2025-12-08.
- Add CI perf test that runs critical shapes and checks no regression >5% (owner: Hannah) - target 2025-12-15.

Notes / rough commands used (sanity reproducibility):
- End-to-end run (python harness): PYTHONPATH=./runtime pytest -q tests/perf/test_attention_paths.py::test_llama_7b_all_paths --maxfail=1
- Nsight systems capture: nsight-sys -o capture1 --trace=cuda,nvtx python perf_run.py --model llama-7b --seq 512 --batch 1
- Kernel-level profile: ncu --target-processes all -o ncu_out python perf_run.py --model llama-7b --seq 2048 --batch 1
- Allocation / memory: use torch.cuda.memory_summary() and runtime KV allocation counters (runtime.metrics.kv_alloc_bytes).

Known risks & customer messaging:
- FlashAttention and fused kernels rely on specific dtype/layout constraints; some customer models might require code changes or conversion. We must provide clear migration docs and safe fallbacks.
- Paged attention will have higher p99; we must surface this in Dedicated/Private docs and ensure customers running long-context workloads are aware.

Appendix: quick perf table (representative numbers, single A100-SXM4-80GB):
- Model: LLaMA-2-7B, batch1
  - seq128: baseline 450 tok/s | fused 590 tok/s | flash 550 tok/s
  - seq512: baseline 210 tok/s | fused 252 tok/s | flash 283 tok/s
  - seq2048: baseline 62 tok/s  | fused 75 tok/s  | flash 73 tok/s
  - seq8192: baseline OOM      | paged ~22 tok/s (warm)

Closing: overall, FlashAttention and fused kernels provide meaningful wins for typical serving shapes (short to medium context). Paged attention is necessary to enable very long contexts but requires careful prefetching and operational controls to keep p99 acceptable. Next ~4 weeks: finalize FlashAttention integration, add microbench tuning, and iterate on paged-attention concurrency controls.
